name: Question 3
problem:
Given that $f(x,y,z)=\frac{z}{\sqrt{1+y-{x}^{2}}}$ and

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{xz}{\sqrt{(1+y-{x}^{2})^{3}}},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=-\frac{z}{2\sqrt{(1+y-{x}^{2})^{3}}},\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+y-{x}^{2}}},
$$

find the set of values $(x,y,z)$ on which all partial derivatives of $f$ exist.
worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y,z)=\frac{z}{\sqrt{1+y-{x}^{2}}}$ is defined only when $1+y-{x}^{2}>0.$ So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}={(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}<y+1}.
$$

As for the partial derivatives, we have the following.

- The function ${f}_{x}=\frac{xz}{\sqrt{(1+y-{x}^{2})^{3}}}$ is defined only when $1+y-{x}^{2}>0.$ So, the domain of ${f}_{x}$ is 

$$
{D}_{{f}_{x}}={(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}<y+1}.
$$

- Similarly, the domain of ${f}_{y}$ and ${f}_{z}$ are the same

$$
{D}_{{f}_{y}}={D}_{{f}_{z}}={(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}<y+1}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partials of $f$ exist on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{x}}\cap {D}_{{f}_{y}}\cap {D}_{{f}_{z}} & ={D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{x}} \\  & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}<y+1}\cap {(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}<y+1} \\  & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}<y+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Given that f(x,y,z)=z1+y−x2 and ∂f∂x=xz(1+y−x2)3,∂f∂y=−z2(1+y−x2)3,∂f∂z=11+y−x2, find the set of values (x,y,z) on which all partial derivatives of f exist.

a
{(x,y,z):x2≠y+1}
b
{(x,y,z):x2>y+1}
c
{(x,y,z):x2≤y+1}
d
{(x,y,z):x2≥y+1}
e
{(x,y,z):x2<y+1}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that f(x,y,z)=z1+y−x2 is defined only when 1+y−x2>0. So, the domain of f is Df={(x,y,z):x2<y+1}.

As for the partial derivatives, we have the following.

  • The function fx=xz(1+y−x2)3 is defined only when 1+y−x2>0. So, the domain of fx is Dfx={(x,y,z):x2<y+1}.

  • Similarly, the domain of fy and fz are the same Dfy=Dfz={(x,y,z):x2<y+1}.

Finally, we conclude that the partials of f exist on the set

Df∩Dfx∩Dfy∩Dfz=Df∩Dfx={(x,y,z):x2<y+1}∩{(x,y,z):x2<y+1}={(x,y,z):x2<y+1}.
